Call script — Georgia roll-off dumpster hauler (Fort Stewart / Hinesville / Savannah area)

Opening:
"Hey, this is Gus Puckett with Knox Jefferson Group — I'm a federal prime contractor. I'm bidding a job at Fort Stewart, two 30-yard roll-off dumpsters for mattress disposal, needed for about two to three weeks in July, roughly 40 total pickups. Do you service Fort Stewart or Hinesville?"
(If yes, continue. If no, ask: "Do you know anyone in that area who might?" — a referral costs you nothing and saves a search.)
The four asks, in order:

Price: "What's your delivery and rental cost for two 30-yard roll-offs, and what's your per-haul price for pickup and disposal?"
Insurance/billing: "You carry general liability and workers' comp, right? And can you invoice after the job rather than needing payment up front?"
Response time: "One thing to flag — when a dumpster's full, I'd need your team able to respond within about 4 hours. Is that workable for you?"
Past experience: "Last thing — have you done any commercial or government hauling work before? Doesn't need to be formal, just something I can reference in my proposal."

Close:
"Perfect — if I win this, the work's yours. My bid's due Monday at 10, so if you can get me a number by 9 AM that'd be a huge help. I'll text you my info right now: 865-888-6487."
If it's a receptionist or dispatcher, not a decision-maker:
"No problem — is there someone who handles commercial quotes I could call directly, or can you have them call me back this morning? It's time-sensitive, bid's due by 10 AM today."

Voicemail (under 25 seconds):
"Hey, this is Gus Puckett, Knox Jefferson Group. I've got a government dumpster job at Fort Stewart — two 30-yard roll-offs, about 40 pickups over a couple weeks. Bidding it this morning, deadline's 10 AM. If you can call me back with a rough price, that'd be a big help — 865-888-6487. Thanks."
Objection handling:

"We only carry up to 20-yard." — "Understood — could two 20-yard units work instead, serviced a bit more frequently? Or do you know a supplier who carries 30-yard I could call?"
"I'd need to see the site first." — "Totally fair. Today I just need a rough number based on the job description — you won't be held to it, and we can firm it up if I win."
"That's a fast turnaround." — "I know, sorry for the short notice — the government just posted it Friday morning. I appreciate whatever you can get me by 9."


This gets you price, insurance, feasibility, and a past-performance line in one call, so a live answer means you're done with that sub and ready to write up the bid. Good luck Monday morning — you've got the whole package staged and ready the second a number comes back.
